site.name: Black Jack Mine
site.location: California Gulch / Left Hand Creek headwaters
site.category: Historic Gold and Silver Mine / Superfund Site
overview: Black Jack Mine was the former name of the Captain Jack Mine, a historic underground gold-and-silver operation in California Gulch near Ward. Mining in the surrounding district began in the 1860s, and a mill was constructed at the site in 1896.

After nearly a century of intermittent activity under multiple owners, mining ended in 1992. Acid mine drainage and metal-bearing waste affected upper Left Hand Creek, leading to federal Superfund listing in 2003 and a long-running cleanup focused on surface waste and the mine-tunnel system.

timeline.text: Gold and silver mining began in the Ward district and expanded through the headwaters of Left Hand Creek.
A mill was constructed at the site later known as the Captain Jack Mill complex.
Mining at the Captain Jack property ended after nearly a century of intermittent activity and multiple operators.
EPA placed the Captain Jack Mill site on the National Priorities List because of acid mine drainage and metal contamination affecting Left Hand Creek.
Surface cleanup consolidated and capped mine waste to reduce contact with tailings and limit erosion into the watershed.
A release of acidic, metal-bearing water from the Big Five tunnel system contributed to a fish kill in upper Left Hand Creek, prompting additional monitoring and treatment work.

moreHistory: The mine lies about 1.5 miles south of Ward at the headwaters of Left Hand Creek in California Gulch. EPA records identify the broader site at 93 California Gulch Road.

The historic property includes the Captain Jack mine and mill area, the Big Five tunnel, and associated waste and water-treatment features. Remnant uses EPA's site coordinate as a complex-level identification point rather than a claim about any one surviving portal.
Cleanup and water-quality monitoring continue through cooperation among EPA, the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, and local watershed partners.
